answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a verifiable history of useful work. Like a terrace built stone by stone, reputation grows only from completed, checked tasks and fades when an identity goes idle. A newcomer has no standing and must cross a threshold before claiming rewards or voting. A comet flood of fake accounts gains nothing, since each shell has zero history, and splitting real work across copies keeps each below the threshold. The attacker must pay time and compute cost per identity, so the delta between one real history and a thousand shells is easy to spot.
